version.changelog: v1.0.1 — declare openclaw as required binary, explicit watcher disclosure, credentials path compatibility note

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose (local IMAP/SMTP mail access) but the inbox watcher spawns the OpenClaw CLI while inheriting process.env (including email credentials) and also forwards email content to the agent CLI — this creates a clear risk of credential and message exposure that is not adequately documented or constrained.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included code: imap.js and smtp.js implement IMAP/SMTP operations, attachment parsing, and a setup helper that writes a local credentials file. Requiring node/npm/openclaw is coherent because the watcher uses the OpenClaw CLI for alerts. Dependencies (imap, nodemailer, mailparser, pdf-parse, xlsx) are proportional to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and scripts instruct storing credentials in ~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env (loaded via dotenv) and running an optional email watcher that analyzes messages and, when configured, calls the OpenClaw CLI (agent/message send) to deliver alerts. The watcher loads imap.js (which populates process.env with IMAP/SMTP secrets) and later executes openclaw with env: process.env — this means IMAP/SMTP credentials and any other environment variables are passed to the child process. The watcher also crafts an analysis prompt and sends email content to the OpenClaw agent CLI, which may send data to external services. The skill does not clearly warn users that sensitive email content and credentials may be forwarded outside the local process.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote download/install spec is present; package.json and package-lock.json list standard public NPM dependencies. No suspicious external URLs or archives are used. The setup.sh helper only writes local credential files and runs local tests.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill stores expected mail credentials in a local dotenv file rather than requiring platform-level env vars, which is reasonable for a mail tool. However, the email-watch implementation passes the entire process.env to child processes (openclaw), exposing IMAP/SMTP credentials (IMAP_PASS, SMTP_PASS, etc.) and any other env variables. That exposure is disproportionate and risky. ALLOWED_READ_DIRS / ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS are present and enforced in code, which is good.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and doesn't modify system-wide or other skill configurations. setup.sh writes a credentials file under ~/.openclaw/credentials and sets mode 600 — expected for this skill. The watcher writes state under workspace memory and uses a local lock file; no privileged escalation or persistent background service is requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements local IMAP/SMTP access and attachment parsing as advertised, but exercise caution before installing or enabling the optional inbox watcher. The watcher: (1) loads your IMAP/SMTP credentials into process.env (from ~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env), and (2) runs the OpenClaw CLI with env: process.env and a prompt that can include message content — so both your mailbox contents and your credentials could be exposed to the OpenClaw CLI/agent and any remote services it contacts. Before installing, consider: - Only use this with a throwaway/test mailbox or accounts with minimal privileges. - If you plan to use the watcher, audit whether your OpenClaw CLI/agent sends data to an external service and whether you trust that destination. - Prefer disabling the watcher entirely if you don't need automated forwarding; you can still run imap.js/smtp.js manually. - If you will use the watcher, modify email-watch-lite.js to sanitize the environment passed to execFileSync (pass a minimal env object without IMAP_*/SMTP_* secrets) or send only minimal alert metadata (not raw message content). - Keep ALLOWED_READ_DIRS and ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS tight and verify they are set in the credentials file. - Review code (especially email-watch-lite.js) and test in an isolated environment before giving it access to real credentials. If you want, I can suggest a concrete patch to prevent environment leakage when invoking openclaw.
llm.findings:
[child_process_exec] expected: email-watch-lite.js uses execFileSync to invoke the OpenClaw CLI to send alerts; invoking a CLI is expected for forwarding alerts, but it is done while passing process.env which includes loaded credentials — that raises a credential-leak risk.
[dotenv_loads_env] expected: imap.js and smtp.js load a credentials file with dotenv. This is expected for a local email tool, but combined with the child-process behavior it means secrets are available in process.env and may be propagated to children.
